payload.root_cause: In `slugify` (src/text.js:11), the call `title.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` is missing the `g` (global) flag on the regex. Without `g`, `String.prototype.replace` substitutes only the first match of a run of whitespace/dashes. For input 'Hello Big  World!', after lowercasing, trimming, and stripping non-slug characters (which removes '!'), the string is 'hello big  world'; the non-global replace converts only the first whitespace run (the single space after 'hello') into '-', yielding 'hello-big  world' — the double space between 'big' and 'world' is left intact instead of also being collapsed to a single dash, so the function fails to join every word with dashes as documented. The correct behavior requires `/[\s-]+/g` so all whitespace/dash runs are each replaced with one dash.

src/text.js:3-4 documents slugify as producing 'words joined by single dashes', which the implementation violates for any input with more than one whitespace/dash run.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the missing `g` (global) flag on the regex `/[\s-]+/` in `slugify` (src/text.js:11). Without it, `String.prototype.replace` only substitutes the first run of whitespace/dashes, leaving subsequent runs (e.g. the double space between 'big' and 'world') intact, producing 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. Adding the `g` flag makes the replacement apply to every whitespace/dash run, collapsing each into a single dash, which matches the documented behavior 'words joined by single dashes' and satisfies both test cases (including '  Already-slugged  title ' where the first matched run is a no-op '-'). This is the minimal change: one character added, consistent with the sibling global replacements on lines 10 and 12.
